y0: The Spirit Led Him to the Wilderness
y1: It was the Holy Spirit who led Jesus into the wilderness. The temptation was not an accident outside of God's plan.
y2: Jesus fasted for 40 days and 40 nights. Israel was tested in the wilderness for 40 years and often failed. Jesus walks that same path again and overcomes where Israel fell.
y3: All three of Jesus' answers are from chapters 6–8 of the book of Deuteronomy. These are the words Moses spoke to Israel as he looked back at their 40 years in the wilderness. Jesus rewrote Israel's story of failure into a story of obedience.
y5: The devil says, “If You are the Son of God, command these stones to become bread.” Hunger itself is not a sin. The temptation was to meet His own needs by His own power without trusting the Father.
y6: Jesus answered, “Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds out of the mouth of God”.
y7: “If You are the Son of God” are words that plant doubt. Just moments before, the Father had called Him the “beloved Son.” Temptation often comes in the form of “prove it.” Jesus didn't try to prove anything.
y8: The Second and Third Temptations · Proof and Power
y9: On the roof of the temple, the devil quotes Psalm 91 and challenges Jesus to throw Himself down. The devil can quote the Bible too. Jesus answered, “You shall not test the Lord your God”.
y10: Finally, the devil says he will give Him all the kingdoms of the world if He worships him. This was a shortcut to glory without the cross. Jesus said, “Go away, Satan! You shall worship the Lord your God, and Him only shall you serve”.
y12: The devil left, and angels came and served Jesus. The help of the angels, which He refused in the temptation to jump from the temple, came as a gift at the end of His obedience.
y13: Jesus was tempted in all points like we are, yet without sin. Because of this, He is able to help us when we are tempted.
y14: The devil also quoted the Word. What matters is not knowing many verses, but trusting God within the whole flow of the Word. Before Jesus used the Word as a weapon, He lived by it.
verse: “Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds out of the mouth of God.”
prayer: Dear Lord God, I praise Jesus who overcame temptation in the wilderness in our place. When I hear the voice saying “prove it,” help me to remember that I am already a loved child. Help me not just to know the Word, but to live by it. I pray in the name of Jesus Christ, who overcame. Amen.
d0: Holy Spirit. The Spirit who descended at His baptism immediately led Jesus to the place of temptation. After receiving power, His first destination was not a stage, but the wilderness.
d1: devil. It means “to divide, to accuse.” The Hebrew word “Satan” means “adversary.” The devil is called the father of lies (John 8:44).
d2: temple. The Jerusalem temple that Herod greatly rebuilt. The southeast corner was about 45 meters high above the valley. The “roof of the temple” was probably that corner.
d3: worship. This is exactly what the wise men did to Jesus in the second lesson. The devil wanted this for himself. Jesus said that we must worship only God.
d4: temptation. It means “to test, to try.” It refers both to trials that strengthen faith and to enticements that lead to sin. The Lord's Prayer also says, “bring us not into temptation” (6:13).
d5: Deuteronomy. The book where Moses retaught the law to Israel after 40 years in the wilderness, before entering the promised land. All three of Jesus' answers are from this book.
